run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The only change applied to the astronomy-shop application during the window is a configuration-only rollout of the frontend-proxy Deployment: helm created it at 2026-11-23T21:37:37Z, then an update by manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 21:38:59Z bumped it to generation 2 and replaced ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 with frontend-proxy-88764bfbb (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy unchanged). Every other Deployment is generation 1 with only helm plus kube-controller-manager entries (fact). The frontend-proxy container runs an inline Perl 'edge request filter' that evaluates the user-controlled `waf` query parameter against WAF_RULE_REGEX="^([a-zA-Z]+)*$" with WAF_RULE_ENABLED="true" inside a single sequential accept() loop and forwards to frontend:8080; it is the only workload in the namespace carrying any WAF_* setting, and every storefront request passes through it (load-generator -> frontend-proxy spans -> frontend) (facts). That regex/quantifier combination is a textbook catastrophic-backtracking (ReDoS) pattern evaluated on untrusted input in a process that handles one connection at a time, so the supported hypothesis is that the modified frontend-proxy is the faulty component and that a long non-matching `waf` value would stall all storefront traffic. The fault itself was NOT observed firing: trace data ends at ~21:39:02, before the new pod was serving, and the new frontend-proxy pod logged nothing in the window, so no post-change latency/error impact of this fault is evidenced (partial). Separately, the ad service showed real error spans at 21:38:40–21:38:54 (flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean, rpc.grpc.status_code=4 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, ~501 ms each) which inflated GET /api/data to ~1.52 s and pushed locust p95 to 1500 ms with one HTTP 500 on POST /api/cart; this burst cleared by the 21:39:07 locust snapshot (p95 56 ms) and coincides with flagd starting at 21:38:16, 32 s after the ad pod, so it is treated as a startup transient, not the injected fault. All pods are Running/Ready with zero restarts, Services have endpoints, no NetworkPolicies or Ingresses exist, and all flagd feature flags in flagd-config are at defaultVariant 'off' (facts).

claims.text: All 27 pods in namespace astronomy-shop were Running with all containers ready and 0 restarts at query time, including frontend-proxy-88764bfbb-79c9z; all 23 Deployments reported 1 ready replica.

Deployment frontend-proxy (namespace astronomy-shop) was created by manager 'helm' at 2026-11-23T21:37:37Z, then updated by manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 2026-11-23T21:38:59Z, reaching generation 2, with a controller status update at 21:39:04Z; every other Deployment in the namespace is generation 1 with only helm and kube-controller-manager entries.

The frontend-proxy container spec is an inline Perl script run as ['/usr/bin/perl','-e'] that reads a candidate from the `waf=` query parameter, and when WAF_RULE_ENABLED is not 'false' evaluates `$candidate =~ /$rule/` with $rule from WAF_RULE_REGEX, then logs {"event":"request_filter_eval",..."elapsedSeconds":...}; it accepts and handles one client at a time in a single accept() loop and proxies to FRONTEND_HOST=frontend:8080 with a 5 s upstream connect timeout and a 1 s read-select loop.

The settings in effect on that container are WAF_RULE_REGEX="^([a-zA-Z]+)*$" and WAF_RULE_ENABLED="true" (on, not off/false); frontend-proxy is the only Deployment in the namespace with any WAF_* setting — all other Deployments expose only FLAGD_HOST=flagd and FLAGD_PORT=8013 style variables.

Events in astronomy-shop record the rollout: ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-88764bfbb 'Created pod: frontend-proxy-88764bfbb-79c9z' at 21:38:59Z with container started 21:39:03Z, Deployment 'Scaled up replica set frontend-proxy-88764bfbb from 0 to 1' at 21:38:59Z, then 'Scaled down replica set frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 from 1 to 0' and 'Stopping container frontend-proxy' on the old pod at 21:39:04Z.

Service frontend-proxy selects opentelemetry.io/name=frontend-proxy on port 8080 and its only endpoint address is pod frontend-proxy-88764bfbb-79c9z at 10.244.234.142; every other astronomy-shop Service also has a populated endpoint pointing at its single pod.

Trace evidence shows user traffic passing through the proxy: load-generator span 'user_get_ads'/'GET' -> frontend-proxy spans 'GET' + 'router frontend egress' -> frontend 'GET /api/data' -> ad 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds', with the frontend-proxy 'GET' span lasting 1,518,055 us in trace 304f27ec707457c23c916acab1e13c6a.

In the 21:38:40–21:38:55 samples the ad service emitted 12 error spans on operation 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean' with status tags error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED), all ~501 ms, while its parent 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' spans took ~1.51 s and frontend 'GET /api/data' took ~1.52 s.

The locust-fetcher log at 21:38:57Z reported fail_ratio 0.012048 with one error "HTTPError('500 Server Error: Internal Server Error for url: /api/cart')" on POST /api/cart, p95 1500 ms and POST /api/checkout max 587 ms; the 21:39:07Z sample reported no errors, p95 56 ms, and the 21:39:19Z gauge sample reported aggregated current_rps 4 with 10 locust users.

The flagd pod started its containers at 21:38:16Z and logged 'Flag IResolver listening at [::]:8013' plus 'watching filepath: ./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json', while the ad pod had already started at 21:37:44Z.

Every feature flag in ConfigMap flagd-config has defaultVariant 'off' (llmInaccurateResponse, llmRateLimitError, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad, failedReadinessProbe, emailMemoryLeak); the ConfigMap was created by helm at 21:37:37Z and has no later manager entry.
At query time the namespace contained zero NetworkPolicy objects and the cluster contained zero Ingress objects, so connection failures are not explained by those resources as they exist now.

Primary hypothesis: the frontend-proxy Deployment now runs a single-threaded Perl edge proxy whose enabled WAF rule "^([a-zA-Z]+)*$" is evaluated on the attacker/user-controlled `waf` query value; a long candidate that ends in a non-letter forces catastrophic backtracking, blocking the one accept() loop and therefore every storefront request (latency, hangs, 502 from the 5 s upstream timeout). The setting is on (WAF_RULE_ENABLED="true"), it belongs to the workload that was just rolled out with an unchanged image, and no other object was seen applying a change or fault.

Secondary hypothesis: the ad service's flagd ResolveBoolean DEADLINE_EXCEEDED burst (21:38:40–21:38:54) is a startup transient — the ad pod started at 21:37:44 while flagd only began listening on 8013 at 21:38:16, so the gRPC channel was backing off — and it had cleared by the 21:39:07 locust sample (p95 56 ms, no errors), so it is not the persistent injected fault.

Rejected: an active flagd feature-flag fault (e.g. adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, failedReadinessProbe, emailMemoryLeak) caused the observed errors — every flag in flagd-config still has defaultVariant 'off' and the ConfigMap has no post-helm modification.

Rejected as workload damage: the frontend-proxy pod change was a controller/rollout replacement (Deployment scaled the new ReplicaSet up and the old one to 0, new pod name, restart count 0), not a crash, eviction or OOM; its readiness at start is not impact.

Nothing in the window shows a crash, restart or unavailable pod: all 27 pods were Running/Ready with 0 restarts, every Service had its endpoint, and the locust gauge at 21:39:19 showed aggregated current_rps 4, 10 users and fail_ratio 0 — so the storefront was serving traffic at the end of the window.

Compare the current frontend-proxy pod template (command/args and WAF_RULE_REGEX/WAF_RULE_ENABLED) against the chart's source of truth for the release, and restore the unmodified Envoy/edge-proxy image and settings; treat any enabled WAF rule with a nested-quantifier regex such as ^([a-zA-Z]+)*$ on a user-controlled query parameter as the fault to be removed rather than tuned.

Reproduce before/after the rollout: capture the load generator's exact request URLs to see whether a `waf` parameter is sent, and watch frontend-proxy container CPU, the per-request 'request_filter_eval' elapsedSeconds log line, and frontend-proxy request latency/error rate; a single-threaded proxy saturating its 100m CPU limit with rising elapsedSeconds would confirm the backtracking mechanism.

gaps: The fault was not observed firing: the trace sample ends at ~21:39:02.9 (source_end_at of the frontend-proxy trace query) and the new frontend-proxy pod (frontend-proxy-88764bfbb-79c9z, started 21:39:03Z) produced zero readable log lines in the window, so no post-rollout latency or error evidence for the frontend-proxy exists (the empty log read is no_data, not proof that nothing was logged — Perl block-buffers stdout).

The change_history integration is not configured for this Run, so the previous value of the frontend-proxy pod template (command/args and WAF_* variables before 21:38:59Z) cannot be read and the exact field changed by the 'OpenAPI-Generator' update cannot be verified; managedFieldsSummary only gives the write time, not the diff.
The previous frontend-proxy pod (frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-5v75w) was deleted at 21:39:04Z and its logs are unavailable, so its pre-change behaviour cannot be compared.

It is unknown whether the load generator ever sends a `waf` query parameter; the locust request URLs visible in the captured metrics/logs (e.g. /api/data/?contextKeys=..., /api/products/<id>, /api/cart, /api/checkout) show no such parameter, so the trigger condition for the backtracking was not observed.

Application trace metrics (traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_*) returned no samples for the window, so per-service error rates and latency trends could not be computed; absence of those series is unknown, not zero.
The locust series are pushgateway gauges with only a single sample at 21:39:19Z in the window, so the 21:38:57 p95 of 1500 ms and the 1.2% fail ratio cannot be baselined against pre-incident traffic.

Only 20 traces were requested from Jaeger for the error-tagged ad query and the frontend-proxy list was a biased sample (333 of 433 spans omitted in the slice read); the sample does not establish a complete call graph or an error rate.

The Redis/Valkey target reported SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so the cart backend used by POST /api/cart (which returned one HTTP 500 at 21:38:57Z) could not be inspected; the 500 is unassigned beyond the frontend/load-generator view.

The load-generator itself has no pod in the cluster (locust-fetcher and load-generator appear only in Loki labels and pushgateway series), so its configuration and start time are not verifiable from Kubernetes state.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
